Christian, who lost her father at the age of four, will enjoy the scholarship through the Alex Otti Foundation. Otti announced the gesture while hosting the victorious students at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, where he also awarded ₦1 million each to the five students who represented Abia State and Nigeria at the international competition. Vanguard learnt that the motorists had looked forward to having the CNG buses in the last three months despite the huge cost incurred in converting their vehicle engines from Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) to the more affordable and eco-friendly CNG they have not been able to get the product. The protesters lamented that the shortage has defeated the aim of converting their vehicles to CNG as a cost-saving measure. They complained that when they stormed the the NNPC Mega Station along the Western Bypass axis that they were frustrated over the prolonged shortage. Vanguard findings have shown that a component of the CNG dispensing machine at the station developed a fault and was left unattended to, leaving motorists with CNG engines in the entire state capital with no alternative but to rely on the more expensive PMS. This persistent shortage has imposed additional financial burdens on vehicle owners, who now face increased transportation costs while struggling to keep their vehicles running. A motorists, Engr. item.title: Inter rally late to down Fiorentina and regain Serie A lead
item.description: Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina at San Siro on Sunday and return to the summit of Serie A. Alex Jimenez’s rocket strike had the struggling visitors heading for a shock win, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute. The result meant the Nerazzurri returned to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club’s winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot. Cristian Chivu’s side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, who made a fingertip stop on a Pio Esposito header before showing quick reactions to parry Thuram’s angled drive. De Gea was alert again to parry a fierce Thuram strike over the bar early in the second half, but it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes. Former AC Milan player Alex Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner. Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser, with Carlos Augusto’s glancing header coming off the top of the bar and De Gea denying substitute Petar Sucic, but they could not find a way through until the game was into added time. Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner to level the scores before winning a penalty when he was dragged down by Victor Valdepenas in the box, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory. Later on Sunday, Atalanta host Frosinone and Genoa face Venezia before Juventus travel to Lecce and AC Milan go to Udinese. The virus has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years. Photo by TONY KARUMBA / AFP Ebola is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe haemorrhagic fever. item.title: EPL: Carrick benches Bruno Fernandes after Como outburst
item.description: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said it was a “pure football” decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench despite the Portugal midfielder’s criticism of his manager’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como. Without a win in seven games in all competitions, Carrick badly needs a victory against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to quell speculation over his future and has made a bold call. The Red Devils begin the day 15th in the table with just seven points from their opening seven league games. Fernandes hit out at United’s passive approach out of possession as Champions League debutants Como ran riot in Italy on Wednesday. “When you have options it’s always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want,” added Carrick as he dismissed the decision was taken as a response to Fernandes’s outburst. Fernandes won a clean sweep of individual awards last season after breaking the Premier League record for assists with 21 as United finished third in the table. But the 32-year-old’s impact has been much more limited so far this season, bar a hat-trick against Ipswich back in August. Carrick made four changes in total with Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui also dropping out for Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo. Fernandes’s comments came just over a week after Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s board for not doing enough to strengthen Carrick’s squad in the transfer window. Martinez was not dropped for his remarks but was replaced at half-time in a 1-1 draw at Leeds last weekend with an injury and is only fit enough to return from the bench against Bournemouth. “You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players,” said United’s all-time leading goalscorer Wayne Rooney. He added: “These players, they’re selfish. item.title: FRSC identifies persistent safety violations among tanker drivers
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has identified speeding, driver fatigue, overloading and driving against traffic as persistent violations among petroleum tanker drivers. The FRSC spokesman, Osondu Ohaeri who told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Abuja, warned that such practices continue to threaten road safety despite enforcement efforts. Ohaeri further discussed the challenges associated with the transportation of petroleum products and other goods by articulated vehicles. He said some tanker drivers exceeded recommended speed limits in attempts to meet delivery schedules, despite the difficulty of bringing heavily loaded vehicles to a safe stop. He explained that the size and weight of tankers required drivers to exercise caution, particularly when approaching bridges, bends and congested sections of highways. He also identified fatigue as a major risk, noting that some drivers attempted to cover long distances, including journeys from Kano to Lagos, overnight without adequate rest. “Driving while fatigued could impair concentration and reaction time, increasing the likelihood of losing control of vehicles. “Also, driving against traffic is another serious violation. Some operators overload their vehicles or use them to carry additional goods alongside petroleum products. “These practices can compromise vehicle stability and expose drivers, passengers and other road users to danger,” he said. Ohaeri attributed the persistence of the violations partly to drivers’ attitudes and the pressure to meet delivery schedules, stressing that compliance with traffic regulations remained essential regardless of operational demands. He said the FRSC had continued to intensify safety education and enforcement while working with operators and other stakeholders to improve compliance. He disclosed that the corps had achieved about 75 per cent success in issuing the appropriate Class G driver’s licences to relevant operators, as part of efforts to ensure that drivers possessed the required qualifications. He said the agency was also engaging petroleum marketers and other industry stakeholders to strengthen safety standards across the transportation chain. He urged tanker drivers and operators to prioritise safety over delivery schedules, warning that violations involving vehicles conveying highly flammable products could have devastating consequences. He called for improved driver discipline, adequate rest, proper vehicle maintenance and strict adherence to speed limits to reduce crashes involving articulated vehicles. In a separate arrest at Enhere Junction, Warri, a 46-year-old physically challenged woman was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 with 6.0kg of skunk. Meanwhile, a 41-year-old suspect was also arrested on Oct. 19 in Adamasingba, Ibadan, Oyo State, following his initial escape from arrest when NDLEA officers seized 197.8kg of cannabis sativa from his house on Sept. 16. Babafemi said a raid in Gerawa area of Kano on Oct. 22 led to the arrest of a suspect and seizure of 159 blocks of cannabis sativa weighing 97.2kg. Also, NDLEA officers at the Lankaviri checkpoint, Yorro Local Government Area, Taraba, on Oct. 23, arrested another suspect with 95 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 60.175kg. “The same day, the Nigeria Police Force handed over a suspect arrested at Dakka village, Bali LGA, with 112 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 81.49kg,” he said. Similarly, in Niger State, another suspect was arrested by NDLEA operatives on Oct. 19 on Sabo-Kainji road, Borgu LGA, with 64,000 pills of opioids, including tramadol and diazepam. Babafemi said NDLEA officers also arrested another suspect on Oct. 21 at Nasaru Town, Ningi LGA, Bauchi State, where they seized 379kg of cannabis sativa packed in seven jumbo sacks. “Acting on intelligence, NDLEA officers on Oct. 20 raided a farm at Board-Ala, Akure South, Ondo, and recovered 56 bags of abandoned cannabis sativa weighing 583kg. “Two cannabis farms in Ugbada Forest, Uzebba, Owan West LGA, Edo, with an estimated yield of 2,023.14kg, were destroyed on Oct. 18 by NDLEA operatives. “They also burnt 450kg of processed cannabis at the site and took 97kg as exhibit,” he said. They had been there for what felt like ten minutes, carefully picking up one product after another, turning the packs over to read the labels before placing them back. The wife was scrolling through Instagram, almost desperately, as though she hoped someone had recently posted the answer to the question they were trying to solve. “Which milk should we buy?” I couldn’t help but overhear parts of their conversation. Interestingly, they weren’t comparing brands or prices. They were trying to understand the different options available. Should they choose dairy milk or a non-dairy alternative? And if dairy was the right choice, what exactly was the difference between Full Cream Milk and Filled Milk? They wanted to make the right choice but weren’t sure what those terms meant. item.title: Police arrest suspect over railway vandalism in Ogun, recover 16 iron rods
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 36-year-old man, Shobande Taofeek, over alleged vandalism and theft of railway infrastructure in the Arigbajo area of the state. The police also recovered 16 railway iron rods and two gas cylinders suspected to have been stolen during the operation. The arrest was carried out by operatives of the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) unit of the command following intelligence reports about the alleged vandalism and theft of railway materials in the area. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Ogun State Command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said the operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area on Friday October 23, leading to the suspect’s arrest. According to the statement, the suspect subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the recovered items were found. “On 23 October 2026, SWAT operatives intensified surveillance and patrols in the affected area, leading to the suspect’s arrest. He subsequently led the operatives to an uncompleted building where the stolen items were recovered as exhibits,” the statement said. The police further disclosed that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect had allegedly admitted involvement in similar offences on three previous occasions. However, the command said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the alleged crime and identify other individuals who might have been involved. “Efforts are ongoing to apprehend other suspects connected with the crime and recover any additional stolen property,” the statement added. The State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting public assets and critical infrastructure, warning that those responsible for vandalism would be brought to justice. Ojajuni, according to the statement, reaffirmed the command’s “unwavering commitment to protecting public assets, safeguarding critical infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of economic sabotage to justice.” He also called on residents to support security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could help prevent crime and protect public infrastructure across the state. The police urged members of the public to cooperate with law enforcement agencies, stressing the importance of community participation in crime prevention and the maintenance of safer communities. item.title: Real Madrid’s Courtois to miss El Classico due to illness
item.description: Real Madrid have suffered a major setback ahead of their El Clasico clash against Barcelona after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was ruled out of Sunday’s La Liga encounter due to illness. The Belgian goalkeeper has contracted the flu and will miss the Matchday 10 fixture at Camp Nou, forcing Madrid to turn to Ukrainian shot-stopper Andriy Lunin. The development comes at a crucial time for Real Madrid, who trail Barcelona by six points in the La Liga standings and need a positive result to strengthen their title challenge. Real Madrid confirmed Courtois’ late withdrawal in a statement released hours before kick-off. “Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight’s LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu,” the club said. “Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place.” Courtois’ absence represents a significant blow for Madrid, given his importance to the team and his recent performances. The 34-year-old was in action during Madrid’s recent Champions League outing, in which the club reportedly secured a 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig. His late withdrawal leaves Lunin with the responsibility of guarding Madrid’s goal in one of the most important fixtures of the season. Lunin is expected to start in goal in place of Courtois as Madrid prepare to face their fierce rivals. The 27-year-old has served as Courtois’ deputy in recent seasons and gained valuable experience during Madrid’s run to the Champions League final in 2024. He will now face a major test against a Barcelona side that has enjoyed an impressive start to the domestic campaign. Barcelona head into the encounter looking to maintain their strong league form, while Madrid will be eager to close the gap at the top of the standings. Madrid’s preparations have been further complicated by the absence of forward Vinícius Júnior, who remains unavailable as he serves a four-match domestic suspension. The Brazilian’s absence deprives Madrid of an important attacking option for the high-profile encounter. Madrid have also suffered two league defeats this season, against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid, increasing the pressure on the team to secure a result against Barcelona. With Courtois ruled out at the last minute and Vinícius unavailable, Madrid face a difficult challenge as they seek to reduce Barcelona’s six-point advantage in the La Liga title race. item.title: Taraba Govt mobilizes emergency relief, food supplies to Binnari after bandit attack
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Government has deployed emergency relief materials to Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area, less than 24 hours after a deadly bandit raid left more than forty residents dead and several households displaced. The rapid humanitarian intervention was executed on the direct directive of Governor Agbu Kefas, who mandated immediate state assistance to cushion the hardships faced by survivors of the Friday afternoon incursion. A high-powered government delegation led by the Executive Secretary of the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA), Dr. Audu Echuseh, arrived in the community on Saturday to coordinate the distribution of relief items and assess the extent of property destruction. The assessment team included the members representing Karim Lamido Constituencies at the Taraba State House of Assembly, Hon. Anas Shuaibu Didango and Hon. Abner Shittu; the Vice Chairman of Karim Lamido Local Government Council, Alhaji Uba Munyarda; alongside traditional rulers and community stakeholders. Addressing grieving residents during the distribution of supplies which included food grains, mattresses, blankets, and essential non-food items, Dr. Echuseh conveyed Governor Kefas’s deepest condolences to the bereaved families. She stated: “We are here on behalf of the Taraba State Government to show solidarity and provide immediate succour to our brothers and sisters in Binnari. His Excellency has directed that no victim of this dastardly act be left unattended to. “This is just the first phase of our intervention. The government is fully committed to providing necessary humanitarian support while collaborating with security agencies to ensure long-term stability and security in the area.” Reacting to the prompt response, the lawmakers commended the state government for its swift action, pledging total grassroots cooperation with security formations deployed to comb the area and forestall future attacks. Although the police claimed ten persons were killed, residents of the community said more than forty residents were lost to the attack. item.title: ‘My daughter, my biggest priority’ – Naomi Osaka considers quitting tennis
item.description: Former world number one Naomi Osaka cast doubt on her future Sunday saying she would consider quitting tennis if her three-year-old daughter asked her to. The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan took 15 months away from the sport after the birth of her daughter Shai, before returning in 2023. She is in Tokyo to play at the Pan Pacific Open this week and said becoming a mother had reshaped her priorities. “I wouldn’t say I’m part-timing it but my entire day doesn’t consist of that,” said the 29-year-old, now ranked 19 in the world. “It’s tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I’m going to play. “Because if my daughter did say she didn’t want me to travel as much, I’m not the type of person to ignore that.” Osaka also stepped away from tennis in 2021 to prioritise her mental health. She said her “mindset is changing a lot” with age. “My daughter is my biggest priority,” she said. “I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis. “If I think about it in certain ways, I’m really proud of where I am now because it’s not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport.” – Online abuse – Osaka said juggling her duties as a player and a mother was something she was “figuring out little by little”. She also offered support to the American Coco Gauff, who said she had received an “insane” amount of racist abuse on the internet at this month’s China Open. World number five Gauff, who is Black, said the experience had been “kind of draining”. Osaka, whose mother is Japanese and father from Haiti, said “nobody should have to go through that”. “It’s sad but I’m used to it on my end,” she said. “I feel like for me, I’ve dealt with that my entire career through decisions that I make that seem to make some people upset. It’s tough.” Osaka said efforts made by women’s tennis governing body the WTA to combat social media abuse did not “ever seem to fully work all the way”. “I know that some people are like, OK, if it bothers you that much, stay off social media,” said Osaka. “But sometimes that’s the best way to connect with your fans. “From my end, what I do about it is I don’t really go on social media at all.” Osaka is seeded seven in Tokyo and plays Italy’s Jasmine Paolini in the first round. World number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala are also competing. Osaka said she was “not far off” refinding her best form and was “optimistic for next year”. Ajadi attended the anniversary celebration and ₦250 million fundraising ceremony, where other APM candidates and political leaders joined him in expressing support for the community’s development aspirations. He also pledged to support the community’s request for a healthcare centre if elected to the Senate in 2027. item.title: 2027: Tinubu has lost touch with reality, unaware he’s president — Shaibu
item.description: The Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, has accused President Bola Tinubu of losing touch with reality, alleging that he is disconnected from the economic hardship facing Nigerians. Shaibu made the allegation during an interview on ARISE News on Sunday, faulting the president for blaming the opposition for hunger despite spending three and a half years in office. “He has lost touch with reality. Bola is not aware of his environment. He is not aware of what Nigerians are going through. He’s not even aware that he’s president,” Shaibu said. He described Tinubu’s explanation of the country’s hunger crisis as delusional, arguing that the president should take responsibility for the economic situation under his administration. “I watched him yesterday and my eight-year-old son who was beside me said, what’s this man talking about? He has been in office for three and a half years. And he’s talking about hunger being created by the opposition. I think it is delusional,” he said. Shaibu challenged Tinubu to compare the cost of living when he assumed office on May 29, 2023, with the current situation, arguing that Nigerians should not be worse off under his leadership. He cited the removal of petrol subsidy as a major factor behind rising prices, saying the policy triggered sharp increases in the cost of goods and services. “Bola Tinubu claimed the podium, and announced that subsidy was gone. And boom, what happened? Everything rose astronomically. The Nigerians cannot afford three square meals today,” he said. The ADC campaign official also alleged that higher university fees had forced some students out of school, despite the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). He further criticised Tinubu for continuing to blame the opposition, noting that the All Progressives Congress governed the country for eight years under former President Muhammadu Buhari before handing over power in 2023. Shaibu said Tinubu’s remarks on hunger raised questions about his understanding of the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians. He argued that the president should be held accountable for his administration’s economic policies rather than attributing the crisis to political opponents.
